subject.declared_domain: The C2/C3-in-graph MATERIALIZE SPEC writer: emits proposed node + CONTAINS-edge records (C2Motif class nodes, C3System nodes, C3->C2 and C2->C1 CONTAINS edges) as ONE json artifact for 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps to ingest into the estate graph. It is a SPEC EMITTER, not an ingester: it writes no graph, opens no store, and performs no promotion. Its declared domain stops at the file it writes.

methodology.how: A single build_spec() pass over two upstream catalogs plus a decompression ladder. It iterates NFRA_MOTIF_P1_c2_catalog.CATALOG, calls P1.build_motif(spec) per entry and RETAINS ONLY those whose recurrence >= P1.AC3_THRESHOLD; the surviving motifs become C2Motif node records. For each it derives the C1 layer via comp_ladder.decompress(motif) filtered to layer=='C1', canonicalises each C1 nid by stripping the ladder discriminator, DEDUPES by canonical target while merging the detector provenance into props.via_detectors, and emits one C2->C1 CONTAINS edge per distinct target. It then loads the cluster index and shares-source from NFRA_MOTIF_P2_c3_emergence, builds C3 systems over the retained motif nodes, and emits a C3System node plus one C3->C2 CONTAINS edge per member. The return is a single dict carrying producer/consumer/cert/grounding strings, a convention_note, a taxonomy_prereq block, a counts block and the nodes and edges arrays; main() serialises it with json.dump(indent=2).

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: TWO DIFFERENT PLANES, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS GUARDED. (a) BEFORE THE OPEN: if build_spec() raises P1.GraphUnavailable, main() catches it at :154, prints the fail-closed notice, RETURNS EXIT CODE 2, and never reaches the write -- the previous motif_c2c3_materialize.json is preserved intact. Any other exception raised inside build_spec() is also pre-open: it propagates as an uncaught traceback and the artifact is untouched. (b) ON THE WRITE PLANE, UNGUARDED: :160 opens SPEC_ARTIFACT with mode 'w', which TRUNCATES the last-good file at the open, and only then does :161 call json.dump. A serialization error, a short or failed write, an encoding error, or an interruption after the open leaves the artifact EMPTY OR PARTIAL, with no temp-file-and-rename and no read-back to recover from. The fail-closed guarantee covers (a) and does NOT extend to (b).
silent_degrade_paths: THE UNGUARDED WRITE PLANE (:160-161): open(mode='w') truncates before json.dump runs, so a failure between the two destroys the last-good artifact rather than preserving it. The module has no write-to-temp-then-rename and no post-write read-back. This is the one path where the subject's own stated requirement -- that a partial or empty spec must not be silently ingested (:155-156) -- is NOT enforced by the code that states it, and the artifact is consumed on every derive.

THE GUARDED PATH IS INVISIBLE ON THE ARTIFACT PLANE: after the GraphUnavailable branch fires, the artifact is byte-identical to what not running the script at all produces. Only the exit code and the stdout line separate them, and both are ephemeral -- nothing durable records that a regeneration was attempted and refused.

The emitted artifact carries no emitted_at, no run id and no input vintage: its grounding block pins upstream COMMITS but not the moment or the graph state of the run. A reader of the file alone cannot date it except by filesystem or git metadata external to it.

Because the script has no cadence and no trigger, the GraphUnavailable guard is CORRECT AND UNREACHABLE in the live estate: it protects a regeneration path that nothing invokes. The truncate-then-serialize exposure is dormant for the same reason -- and stops being dormant the moment anyone runs it.
failure_mode.evidence: Read at source :146-170 @c0dc3f09a0. The except clause is :154, the refusal prints :157-158, return 2 at :159. THE WRITE IS :160-161 AND ITS MODE IS THE POINT: open(SPEC_ARTIFACT, 'w', encoding='utf-8') then json.dump(spec, fh, indent=2) -- mode 'w' truncates AT THE OPEN, so the destructive act precedes the serialization and nothing re-establishes the prior content if the serialization does not complete. THAT WAS FALSE, and it was an overclaim on the exact axis this row exists to measure. distinguishable_from_true_negative stays 'no' because it is scored on the GUARDED path, where the post-failure artifact is byte-identical to the never-run state; the unguarded write-plane failure is a different and worse outcome (a corrupt or empty artifact) and is recorded in silent_degrade_paths rather than folded into this scalar. NOT EXERCISED: neither branch was induced -- GraphUnavailable would require making the graph unreachable and the write-plane failure would require interrupting a write, both outside this TO's no-deploy/no-infra scope. Both are READ, not RUN, and this row says so rather than implying an exercise.

verdict.why: The script does several careful things well: it canonicalises across two identity spaces with the conversion verified at the store, and it preserves detector provenance through a dedupe that would otherwise lose it. What qualifies it is a gap between what it guards and what it claims to guard, plus a gap between what it is and how the estate uses it. FOUR QUALIFYING FACTS, each measured above: (1) THE FAIL-CLOSED GUARANTEE IS NARROWER THAN THE CODE'S OWN COMMENT CLAIMS -- :155-156 says a partial or empty spec would be silently ingested and must be refused, but the guard covers only pre-open failures; the write itself is truncate-then-serialize (:160-161, mode 'w'), so a failure during serialization destroys the last-good artifact instead of preserving it, with no temp-and-rename and no read-back; (2) the script has NO cadence and NO trigger -- nothing invokes it -- while the artifact it wrote in July is read on every derive, so a frozen output is load-bearing and its writer is dormant; (3) on the guarded path the failure mode is not distinguishable from a genuine negative, because the preserved artifact is byte-identical to the never-run state; (4) the artifact carries no self-dating field, so its age is knowable only from metadata outside it. None of these makes the current output wrong -- it was measured correct at 6 / 1 / 36. Together they mean nothing in the system would notice if it became wrong, and one of them means a single interrupted run could make it wrong destructively.
blocking_defects: SUBJECT DEFECT, NOT REMEDIATED HERE (this TO authorises no code change): the write at :160-161 truncates the last-good artifact at open(mode='w') and only then serializes, so any failure on the write plane leaves an empty or partial motif_c2c3_materialize.json -- an artifact consumed on every derive. The module's own comment at :155-156 states the requirement this path violates. The conventional remedy is to serialize to a string or a temp file and rename over the target.
